svg.title: Input handling — okfy security explainer
svg.desc: What enters the tool and the rules every input passes through. Five things enter: the URL's query string, which carries the start file and the depth; the served bundle, which carries Markdown bodies, frontmatter, link destinations and caption tracks; local files from a picked or dropped folder; the preview's own reads of images, audio, video and PDF metadata; and the state kept in this browser, such as the volume, the language and the assistant's settings. Nothing is trusted. The URL's query is checked against the page's own origin and the bundle root before it is used, and a bad value falls back to the default. Bundle paths are normalized, resolved and then validated twice: a destination is decoded exactly once and its encoded separators are refused before the decode, so an encoded separator can never become one; it may not carry a scheme, a backslash, a control character, a query or a fragment; joining it against the file's own directory and each ancestor never climbs above the root; a path is capped at 2048 characters and 24 segments and a dot-directory is skipped; and the resolved URL is re-checked for the same origin, no credentials and a path under the root, then checked a third time on the response's own URL, so a redirect out of the root is refused rather than followed. Alternative candidate paths are tried on a 404 only. Every read is bounded as it streams, before it is buffered: a file is capped at 512 kibibytes, a bundle at 8000 files and 128 mebibytes, the graph at 32 000 nodes and 80 000 links, references at 256 per file, tags at 64, images at eight mebibytes each and sixteen in total, and the renderer has its own input, output, depth and search-work budget; a response's content-length is checked before the body is read and an unused body is cancelled. Untrusted text is escaped where it is written and never re-parsed: text goes through esc for the ampersand, the angle brackets and the double quote; an attribute value goes through markdownAttr, which escapes the single quote too; a link target must be http, https or mailto with no credentials and no control characters, or only its label is written; an image is written with no source and the source is set later through the DOM from a validated blob URL; and raw HTML is never rendered, so an image tag in a bundle is shown as the words a reader sees. Because nothing generated is ever substituted into an attribute, a forged fragment cannot close a quote and become an attribute of its own. The policy is a second line of defence: script-src-attr none means no inline event handler can be created however the markup is built; default-src none means every kind of load must be named, so a new one fails closed; object, base and form actions are off; images come only from the page's own origin, a blob URL or the inline favicon; and connections are limited to the page itself and the assistant's endpoints, which is the documented exception.
svg.text: Nothing the tool reads is trusted: every input is checked before it is used
Five inputs, and the boundary each one is checked at
checked against the page's own origin and the bundle root
before use; a bad value falls back to the default
paths normalized and re-checked after every resolution;
the text rendered with escaping at the sink
read bounded from the File objects; media plays only
from a blob URL of its own bytes
read bounded and validated before use: an image only
from a blob URL, a caption only as plain words
Nothing the tool reads is trusted, and nothing is fetched from a URL it was handed: every request is re-checked
against the bundle root, and only the page's own origin and the bundle folder are ever reached.
A destination is normalized, resolved, and then validated twice
Decoded exactly once: %2f, %5c and %25 are refused before the decode, so an encoded separator can never become
one, and a destination may not carry a scheme, a backslash, a control character, a query or a fragment.
A path is capped at 2048 characters and 24 segments, and a dot-directory is skipped, so nothing hidden is crawled.
The resolved URL is checked again — same origin, no credentials, the path under the root — and checked a third time
on the response's own URL, so a redirect out of the root is refused rather than followed.
Alternative candidate paths are tried on a 404 only, never on another failure, so a miss cannot be turned into a
Every read is bounded as it streams, before it is buffered
512 KiB of text; at the bound the read stops and the rest is cancelled
256 references per file; 64 tags of 256 characters and 16 segments
8 MiB each, 16 MiB in total, 64 per preview
512 KiB in, 2 MiB out, 24 levels deep, 32× the input in search work
A response's content-length is checked before the body is read, and a body that is never used is cancelled.
Untrusted text is escaped where it is written, never re-parsed
escaped for text: & < > and the double quote
escaped for an attribute: the single quote too
http, https or mailto only, with no credentials and no control characters
written with no source; the source is set later from a validated blob URL
never rendered: it is shown as the words a reader sees
Nothing generated is ever substituted into an attribute, so a forged fragment cannot close a quote and become an
attribute of its own — the failure the review's finding A1 describes.
The Content-Security-Policy the page runs under
no inline event handler can be created, however the markup is built
every kind of load must be named, so a new one fails closed
no plugin and no embedded document
a bundle cannot re-point relative URLs or post a form anywhere
images only from the page's own origin, a blob URL or the inline favicon
the page itself and the assistant's endpoints — the documented exception
The rules hold together as one idea: never trust the shape of an input, validate the value that will actually be
used rather than the text that produced it, and escape at the sink where that value is written.
